titulo: Conditionals: zero, first, second, third and mixed
resumen: Zero: if + presente, presente para verdades generales y resultados que siempre se cumplen: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
First: if + presente, will + infinitivo para situaciones reales o probables; nunca will después de if: If it rains tomorrow, we'll have the barbecue indoors.
Second: if + past simple, would + infinitivo para lo irreal o improbable en el presente o el futuro: If I had more time, I'd learn the piano. If I were you, I'd apologise.
Third: if + past perfect, would have + participio para un pasado que no ocurrió: If we'd left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
Mixed: pasado irreal con resultado presente (If I'd taken that job, I'd be living in Madrid now) o rasgo presente con resultado pasado (If I weren't so shy, I'd have spoken to her).
unless = if... not; as long as y provided (that) = solo si; even if = aunque (hipotético); otherwise = si no: You won't get a place unless you apply.
in case no significa «si», sino «por si acaso»: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
If it hadn't been for + sustantivo = «de no haber sido por». Would solo va tras if en peticiones corteses: I'd be grateful if you would send it by Friday.

preguntas.q: If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ green.
preguntas.x: Para una verdad general (zero conditional) se usa presente en las dos partes: If you mix..., you get... Would get sería para una situación imaginaria con if + past, y got no concuerda con mix.

preguntas.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll have the barbecue indoors.
preguntas.x: En el first conditional, la parte con if va en presente aunque hable del futuro: If it rains tomorrow... Will va solo en la otra parte de la oración (we'll have).

preguntas.q: If I ___ more free time, I'd learn to play the piano.
preguntas.x: En el second conditional, la parte con if va en past simple y la otra con would: If I had more time, I'd learn... Would have no se usa después de if, y have no concuerda con I'd.

preguntas.q: I wouldn't sign that contract ___ you.
preguntas.x: If I were you es la forma fija para dar consejos con el second conditional. Would no va tras if, if I am you no tiene sentido porque no es una situación real y if I had been exigiría wouldn't have signed.

preguntas.q: If we ___ earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
preguntas.x: Third conditional: if + past perfect para un pasado que no ocurrió y would have + participio para su resultado. If we left sería second conditional y no concuerda con wouldn't have missed; would have left no va tras if.

preguntas.q: I ___ you if I'd known you were in hospital.
preguntas.x: Si la condición es un pasado irreal (if I'd known), el resultado pasado va con would have + participio. Would visit hablaría del presente, y had visited no puede ir en la parte del resultado.

preguntas.q: You won't get a place on the course ___ you apply before Friday.
preguntas.x: Unless significa if... not: no tendrás plaza si no te inscribes antes del viernes. Con if o as long as la frase diría lo contrario (que inscribirte te deja sin plaza), y in case expresa precaución, no condición.

preguntas.q: Take an umbrella with you now ___ it rains later.
preguntas.x: In case («por si») indica una precaución: lo llevas ahora por si llueve después. If significaría que solo lo llevas si llueve, lo que no encaja con now y later, y otherwise no introduce una condición.

preguntas.q: You can borrow my laptop ___ you're careful with it.
preguntas.x: As long as («siempre que») pone una condición: te lo presto solo si lo cuidas. Unless diría lo contrario, even if («aunque») anularía la condición y so that expresa finalidad.

preguntas.q: You'd better book a table, ___ we won't get in — it's always packed on Saturdays.
preguntas.x: Otherwise («si no», «de lo contrario») introduce lo que pasará si no se hace lo anterior. So that diría que reservamos para no entrar, e in case y even if no tienen ese sentido.

preguntas.q: If I ___ that job in Madrid last year, I'd be living in Spain now.
preguntas.x: Es un mixed conditional: condición en el pasado (last year) con if + past perfect y resultado en el presente (now) con would + infinitivo. If I took hablaría del presente, no de una decisión del año pasado.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: If the weather is good tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
d: If the weather will be good tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
If the weather would be good tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
If the weather will be good tomorrow, we would go hiking.
preguntas.x: En el first conditional no se usa will ni would después de if, aunque se hable del futuro: If the weather is good tomorrow... Will y would van en la parte del resultado.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “You can use the lab at weekends, but only if you book it in advance.”
preguntas.a: You can use the lab at weekends provided that you book it in advance.
d: You can use the lab at weekends unless you book it in advance.
You can use the lab at weekends in case you book it in advance.
You can use the lab at weekends even if you book it in advance.
preguntas.x: Provided (that) equivale a only if: pone una condición necesaria. Unless significa if not y diría lo contrario, mientras que in case y even if no expresan una condición obligatoria.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “I don't have a car, so I can't drive you to the airport.”
preguntas.a: If I had a car, I could drive you to the airport.
d: If I have a car, I can drive you to the airport.
If I had had a car, I could have driven you to the airport.
If I would have a car, I could drive you to the airport.
preguntas.x: Una situación irreal en el presente (no tengo coche) va en second conditional: If I had a car, I could drive you. La primera opción la presenta como posible y la segunda habla del pasado; además, would no va tras if.

preguntas.q: I wouldn't go out with him ___ he were the last man on earth.
preguntas.x: Even if («aunque», hipotético) introduce una condición imaginaria, por eso va con were. Even though solo se usa con hechos reales (even though he is rich), y as long as o in case cambian el sentido.

preguntas.q: If I ___ such a shy person, I would have spoken to her at the party last night.
preguntas.x: Es un mixed conditional: un rasgo permanente del presente (if I weren't such a shy person) con un resultado en el pasado (I would have spoken). Wouldn't be no va tras if, y am not o haven't been no expresan una condición irreal.

preguntas.q: ___ your help, I would never have passed the exam.
d: If it wouldn't have been for
preguntas.x: If it hadn't been for + sustantivo significa «de no haber sido por» y va con would have + participio. Sin for la estructura no funciona, unless no se usa así y would no va tras if.

preguntas.q: I'd be grateful if you ___ me the invoice by Friday.
preguntas.x: Tras if se puede usar would en peticiones formales y corteses: I'd be grateful if you would send... Had sent y have sent hablarían de algo ya hecho, y are sending no forma una petición con I'd be grateful.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “We got lost because we didn't have a map.”
preguntas.a: If we'd had a map, we wouldn't have got lost.
d: If we had a map, we wouldn't get lost.
If we hadn't had a map, we wouldn't have got lost.
If we'd had a map, we wouldn't get lost.
preguntas.x: Un pasado que no ocurrió (no teníamos mapa) se expresa con third conditional: If we'd had a map, we wouldn't have got lost. If we had a map, we wouldn't get lost habla del presente, y la segunda opción invierte el sentido.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: If she hadn't missed the flight, she'd be in Tokyo by now.
d: If she didn't miss the flight, she'd be in Tokyo by now.
If she wouldn't have missed the flight, she'd be in Tokyo by now.
If she hadn't missed the flight, she will be in Tokyo by now.
preguntas.x: Mixed conditional: condición pasada irreal (if she hadn't missed) y resultado presente (she'd be in Tokyo by now). If she didn't miss no sitúa la condición en el pasado, would no va tras if y will no sirve para un resultado irreal.
